fit: diagnostic cohort with visual presence by visit
assessment: Visual symptoms were present in 49 of 67 DLB cases at baseline and 62 at follow-up. In Parkinson disease the counts were 0 and 31 of 111. The comparison counts people. Orange juice was shared in the separate rum challenge on tremor.

fit: drug-induced parkinsonism case after traumatic brain injury
assessment: No auditory or visual hallucinations were observed at rehospitalization. Medication withdrawal relates to the motor syndrome. No repeated visual endpoint or food intervention.
Summarizes visual symptoms as a differentiating feature and links earlier cohorts. No independent episode-frequency measurement or fig exposure.

fit: Lewy body and Parkinson fluctuation comparisons
assessment: Repeated testing distinguishes within-day cognitive variation from objective alertness. These measures do not count formed visual events and were not examined after fig intake.

fit: secondary comparison of EXPRESS, IDEAL and ADENA
assessment: NPI-10 totals and change in the available trials summarize broad behavioral outcomes. Prior trial datasets are reused. No independent food comparison or visual episode rate.
General hallucination adverse-event term was recorded in 17 of 362 on rivastigmine and 17 of 179 on placebo. Modality and per-person event count are unspecified. No food exposure arm.

fit: hospital case series after Ficus insipida latex
assessment: A child in the index case had unconsciousness and edema after a nonculinary latex preparation. The report does not attribute recurrent formed visual episodes to edible dried fig flesh.

Ojé is identified as Ficus insipida and renaco only as Ficus sp. Some plant teachers are described in contexts of dreams, dizziness or visions. No isolated exposure or clinical episode count is reported for dried edible fig.

fit: 2011 ethnography of an attributed ojé spirit encounter
assessment: One account describes the spirit of ojé presenting itself during a dieta. The common name includes F. insipida and F. schultesii. Waking visual modality, species for that account, Parkinson diagnosis and episode frequency remain unspecified.

fit: Alzheimer-model mouse chow with fig material
assessment: Maze escape latency favored the supplemented transgenic group. Preparation mentions dried flesh and an unclear possible extraction step. Neither the tested outcome nor the population measures clinical visual hallucinations.
